attributes.color: Predominantly reddish-brown specks with a few bright yellow dots. The color contrast is sharp against the off-white base of the pill, making the defects visually prominent despite their small scale.
attributes.boundary: The transition between the defect and the normal surface is diffuse and uneven. There is no crisp edge; instead, the specks gradually blend into the pill’s surface, with some overlapping the embossed 'FF' lettering subtly.
attributes.extent: The defect occupies approximately 15% of the pill’s visible surface area, concentrated primarily on the left half. The specks are localized and do not extend across the entire width or length of the pill.

attributes.shape: An irregular, roughly oval-shaped indentation with a partially broken edge on the lower-left side. The defect contains an embossed letter 'F' and a smaller symbol to its right, both appearing slightly misaligned and worn. The overall form suggests material displacement or partial fracture rather than uniform erosion.
attributes.texture: The surface within the defect is matte and uneven, with visible micro-scratches and pitting around the embossed characters. The material appears to be a compressed powder tablet, and the defect area shows signs of mechanical stress with roughened edges and minor flaking near the broken perimeter.
attributes.color: The defect region maintains the same off-white base color as the surrounding tablet but is interspersed with scattered reddish-pink speckles. These speckles are concentrated more densely near the embossed letters and along the fractured edge, suggesting either pigment migration or surface degradation exposing internal components.
attributes.boundary: The boundary between the defect and the intact tablet is uneven and jagged, especially on the lower-left where the material appears torn or chipped. The transition from the damaged area to the undamaged surface is not smooth — it features abrupt height changes and fragmented edges rather than a clean demarcation.
attributes.extent: The defect spans approximately 60% of the tablet’s width and covers about one-third of its length. It is centered horizontally but extends more prominently toward the lower half of the tablet. The damage is localized to this single region without spreading to adjacent areas.

attributes.color: The defect displays a pale off-white hue consistent with the pill’s base color, but the fractured edges reveal subtle reddish-brown flecks embedded in the material, suggesting internal pigment exposure or contamination from the cracking process.
attributes.boundary: The boundary between the defect and intact surface is sharply defined yet irregular, with fragmented edges following the crack’s path. There is no smooth transition — instead, the break exhibits abrupt changes in elevation and material continuity.
attributes.extent: The defect spans nearly the full width of the oval pill, centered horizontally and extending vertically over approximately one-third of its height. It intersects the central 'FF' imprint, disrupting its integrity across both letters.

attributes.shape: An irregular, elongated smudge-like defect located to the right of the embossed 'FF' lettering. It has an amorphous, slightly curved form with no defined geometric structure, appearing as a smeared or rubbed area on the tablet surface.
attributes.texture: The defect exhibits a matte, slightly roughened texture compared to the surrounding smooth tablet surface. Within the smudge, fine granular speckling is visible, suggesting either partial material erosion or embedded particulate matter that disrupts the uniform finish.
attributes.color: The defect displays a reddish-brown hue that contrasts with the white base color of the tablet. The coloration is unevenly distributed, with denser pigmentation concentrated in the center and fading toward the edges, giving it a mottled appearance.
attributes.boundary: The edge between the defect and the unaffected tablet surface is diffuse and indistinct. There is no sharp demarcation; instead, the color gradually blends into the white background, with subtle gradations indicating a soft transition rather than a clean cut.
attributes.extent: The defect spans approximately one-third of the tablet’s width and extends vertically along about half its length. It is localized primarily to the right side of the central 'FF' imprint, not overlapping the letters but adjacent to them.

attributes.shape: The defect appears as a cluster of small, scattered red speckles distributed across the pill's surface. These speckles are irregular in shape, mostly dot-like with some slightly elongated or fragmented forms, and lack any uniform geometric pattern.
attributes.texture: The speckles exhibit a granular texture that contrasts with the smooth, matte white surface of the pill. They appear slightly raised or embedded, giving a minor tactile irregularity compared to the surrounding area, though no deep pits or cracks are visible.
attributes.color: The defect color is a reddish-brown hue, varying slightly in saturation among individual specks. The color stands out against the off-white base material, with no blending or gradient — each speck maintains its distinct pigmentation.
attributes.boundary: The boundary between the speckled defect and the clean pill surface is diffuse and uneven. There is no sharp demarcation; instead, the red particles gradually fade into the white matrix without clear edges, suggesting surface contamination rather than structural damage.
attributes.extent: The defect spans approximately 40% of the pill’s visible surface area, concentrated more densely near the center and extending toward the periphery. The speckles are dispersed in a non-uniform manner, with higher density around the central embossed 'FF' marking.

attributes.shape: An elongated, irregularly shaped indentation with a broken or fractured appearance. The defect features a jagged, uneven outline that interrupts the continuous surface of the tablet, particularly around the lower right portion of the embossed 'FF' lettering.
attributes.texture: The surface within the defect is rough and granular, contrasting with the smoother surrounding tablet material. Small particulate fragments and micro-chips are visible, suggesting mechanical stress or partial disintegration of the tablet's outer layer.
attributes.color: The defect area displays a lighter, off-white hue compared to the slightly pinkish speckled base material. The fragmented regions show subtle variations in tone, with some exposed inner layers appearing more translucent or matte than the intact surface.
attributes.boundary: The boundary between the defect and the surrounding material is sharply defined yet irregular. It exhibits abrupt transitions with no gradual blending — edges appear chipped, torn, or cracked rather than worn smoothly into adjacent areas.
attributes.extent: The defect spans approximately 15–20% of the tablet’s width near the center-right, primarily affecting the lower half of the 'F' characters. It does not extend across the entire length but is concentrated in a localized region where structural integrity appears compromised.

attributes.shape: A roughly circular knot with an irregular, slightly elongated form. The central core is dark and sunken, surrounded by concentric rings of compressed wood fibers that create a textured depression. The overall shape resembles a small, embedded eye or void within the wood grain.
attributes.texture: The defect exhibits a deeply recessed, rough-textured surface compared to the surrounding wood. The center appears charred or decayed, with fibrous material visibly broken and fragmented. Around the perimeter, the wood grain flows inward toward the knot, creating a swirling, uneven texture that contrasts with the smoother adjacent areas.
attributes.color: Predominantly dark brown to black in the center, transitioning to medium brown along the outer rim. The coloration suggests either natural decay or heat damage. Subtle red markings are visible nearby, but they do not blend into the knot’s core — appearing as external stains rather than part of the defect itself.
attributes.boundary: The boundary between the knot and surrounding wood is sharply defined yet irregular. There is no smooth transition; instead, the edge shows abrupt changes in elevation and texture where the grain converges inward. No smudging or blending occurs — the knot stands out distinctly against the lighter wood background.
attributes.extent: The knot occupies approximately 5% of the image area, centered horizontally and slightly below the vertical midpoint. It is flanked by faint red marks on both sides — one to the left and one to the right — which appear unrelated in size and shape to the knot itself, suggesting separate imperfections.

attributes.shape: A localized area of disrupted fabric weave appearing as a small, irregularly shaped void. The defect is vertically oriented and slightly elongated, with an uneven, jagged outline that interrupts the consistent textile pattern.
attributes.texture: The surrounding fabric exhibits a tightly woven, textured surface with uniform interlacing threads. Within the defect, the weave is visibly broken or missing, exposing a smoother, less structured inner layer or underlying material, creating a contrast in surface roughness.
attributes.color: The defect region appears slightly darker than the surrounding fabric due to shadowing from the missing weave structure. attributes.boundary: The edges of the defect are irregular and non-uniform, blending into the intact fabric without sharp demarcation. Some adjacent threads appear frayed or pulled, indicating mechanical stress at the transition zone between damaged and undamaged material.
attributes.extent: The defect spans approximately 5-7mm vertically and occupies less than 1% of the total visible surface area. It is isolated and does not extend horizontally across the fabric strip, remaining confined to a narrow vertical band near the center.
